02.8e479f5ed3:
<n>22:1</n> Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: * in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
<n>22:2</n> Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.
<n>22:3</n> Dedúxit me super sémitas justítiæ, * propter nomen suum.
<n>22:4</n> Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.
<n>22:4</n> Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.
<n>22:5</n> Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.
<n>22:5</n> Impinguásti in óleo caput meum: * et calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est!
<n>22:6</n> Et misericórdia tua subsequétur me * ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
<n>22:6</n> Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini, * in longitúdinem diérum.
02.f102a08b53:
<n>22:1</n> The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. * He hath set me in a place of pasture.
<n>22:2</n> He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment: * he hath converted my soul.
<n>22:3</n> He hath led me on the paths of justice, * for his own name’s sake.
<n>22:4</n> For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, * for thou art with me.
<n>22:4</n> Thy rod and thy staff, * they have comforted me.
<n>22:5</n> Thou hast prepared a table before me * against them that afflict me.
<n>22:5</n> Thou hast anointed my head with oil; * and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it!
<n>22:6</n> And thy mercy will follow me * all the days of my life.
<n>22:6</n> And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord * unto length of days.
02.a85a812e9e:
<n>24:1</n> Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam.
<n>24:3</n> Neque irrídeant me inimíci mei: * étenim univérsi, qui sústinent te, non confundéntur.
<n>24:4</n> Confundántur omnes iníqua agéntes * supervácue.
<n>24:4</n> Vias tuas, Dómine, demónstra mihi: * et sémitas tuas édoce me.
<n>24:5</n> Dírige me in veritáte tua, et doce me: * quia tu es, Deus, salvátor meus, et te sustínui tota die.
<n>24:6</n> Reminíscere miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, * et misericordiárum tuárum, quæ a sǽculo sunt.
<n>24:7</n> Delícta juventútis meæ, * et ignorántias meas ne memíneris.
<n>24:7</n> Secúndum misericórdiam tuam meménto mei tu: * propter bonitátem tuam, Dómine.
<n>24:8</n> Dulcis et rectus Dóminus: * propter hoc legem dabit delinquéntibus in via.
<n>24:9</n> Díriget mansuétos in judício: * docébit mites vias suas.
<n>24:10</n> Univérsæ viæ Dómini, misericórdia et véritas, * requiréntibus testaméntum ejus et testimónia ejus.
<n>24:11</n> Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, propitiáberis peccáto meo: * multum est enim.
<n>24:12</n> Quis est homo qui timet Dóminum? * legem státuit ei in via, quam elégit.
<n>24:13</n> Ánima ejus in bonis demorábitur: * et semen ejus hereditábit terram.
<n>24:14</n> Firmaméntum est Dóminus timéntibus eum: * et testaméntum ipsíus ut manifestétur illis.
<n>24:15</n> Óculi mei semper ad Dóminum: * quóniam ipse evéllet de láqueo pedes meos.
<n>24:16</n> Réspice in me, et miserére mei: * quia únicus et pauper sum ego.
<n>24:17</n> Tribulatiónes cordis mei multiplicátæ sunt: * de necessitátibus meis érue me.
<n>24:18</n> Vide humilitátem meam, et labórem meum: * et dimítte univérsa delícta mea.
<n>24:19</n> Réspice inimícos meos quóniam multiplicáti sunt, * et ódio iníquo odérunt me.
<n>24:20</n> Custódi ánimam meam, et érue me: * non erubéscam quóniam sperávi in te.
<n>24:21</n> Innocéntes et recti adhæsérunt mihi: * quia sustínui te.
<n>24:22</n> Líbera, Deus, Israël, * ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus suis.
02.12f2ff7394:
<n>24:1</n> To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul: * In thee, O my God, I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.
<n>24:3</n> Neither let my enemies laugh at me: * for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.
<n>24:4</n> Let all them be confounded that act unjust things * without cause.
<n>24:4</n> Shew, O Lord, thy ways to me, * and teach me thy paths.
<n>24:5</n> Direct me in thy truth, and teach me; * for thou art God my Saviour; and on thee have I waited all the day long.
<n>24:6</n> Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion; * and thy mercies that are from the beginning of the world.
<n>24:7</n> The sins of my youth * and my ignorances do not remember.
<n>24:7</n> According to thy mercy remember thou me: * for thy goodness’ sake, O Lord.
<n>24:8</n> The Lord is sweet and righteous: * therefore he will give a law to sinners in the way.
<n>24:9</n> He will guide the mild in judgment: * he will teach the meek his ways.
<n>24:10</n> All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth, * to them that seek after his covenant and his testimonies.
<n>24:11</n> For thy name’s sake, O Lord, thou wilt pardon my sin: * for it is great.
<n>24:12</n> Who is the man that feareth the Lord? * He hath appointed him a law in the way he hath chosen.
<n>24:13</n> His soul shall dwell in good things: * and his seed shall inherit the land.
<n>24:14</n> The Lord is a firmament to them that fear him: * and his covenant shall be made manifest to them.
<n>24:15</n> My eyes are ever towards the Lord: * for he shall pluck my feet out of the snare.
<n>24:16</n> Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me; * for I am alone and poor.
<n>24:17</n> The troubles of my heart are multiplied: * deliver me from my necessities.
<n>24:18</n> See my abjection and my labour; * and forgive me all my sins.
<n>24:19</n> Consider my enemies for they are multiplied, * and have hated me with an unjust hatred.
<n>24:20</n> Keep thou my soul, and deliver me: * I shall not be ashamed, for I have hoped in thee.
<n>24:21</n> The innocent and the upright have adhered to me: * because I have waited on thee.
<n>24:22</n> Deliver Israel, O God, * from all his tribulations.
02.cb15a3631e:
<n>26:1</n> Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?
<n>26:1</n> Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?
<n>26:2</n> Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, * ut edant carnes meas:
<n>26:2</n> Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, * ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.
<n>26:3</n> Si consístant advérsum me castra, * non timébit cor meum.
<n>26:3</n> Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, * in hoc ego sperábo.
<n>26:4</n> Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, * ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
<n>26:4</n> Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, * et vísitem templum ejus.
<n>26:5</n> Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: * in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.
<n>26:6</n> In petra exaltávit me: * et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.
<n>26:6</n> Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo ejus hóstiam vociferatiónis: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.
<n>26:7</n> Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: * miserére mei, et exáudi me.
<n>26:8</n> Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: * fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.
<n>26:9</n> Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: * ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.
<n>26:9</n> Adjútor meus esto: * ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
<n>26:10</n> Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: * Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.
<n>26:11</n> Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: * et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.
<n>26:12</n> Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: * quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
<n>26:13</n> Credo vidére bona Dómini * in terra vivéntium.
<n>26:14</n> Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: * et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.
02.4616cc3b6b:
<n>26:1</n> The Lord is my light and my salvation, * whom shall I fear?
<n>26:1</n> The Lord is the protector of my life: * of whom shall I be afraid?
<n>26:2</n> Whilst the wicked draw near against me, * to eat my flesh.
<n>26:2</n> My enemies that trouble me, * have themselves been weakened, and have fallen.
<n>26:3</n> If armies in camp should stand together against me, * my heart shall not fear.
<n>26:3</n> If a battle should rise up against me, * in this will I be confident.
<n>26:4</n> One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; * that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.
<n>26:4</n> That I may see the delight of the Lord, * and may visit his temple.
<n>26:5</n> For he hath hidden me in his tabernacle; * in the day of evils, he hath protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle.
<n>26:6</n> He hath exalted me upon a rock: * and now he hath lifted up my head above my enemies.
<n>26:6</n> I have gone round, and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: * I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.
<n>26:7</n> Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to thee: * have mercy on me and hear me.
<n>26:8</n> My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: * thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.
<n>26:9</n> Turn not away thy face from me; * decline not in thy wrath from thy servant.
<n>26:9</n> Be thou my helper, * forsake me not; do not thou despise me, O God my Saviour.
<n>26:10</n> For my father and my mother have left me: * but the Lord hath taken me up.
<n>26:11</n> Set me, O Lord, a law in thy way, * and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.
<n>26:12</n> Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; * for unjust witnesses have risen up against me; and iniquity hath lied to itself.
<n>26:13</n> I believe to see the good things of the Lord * in the land of the living.
<n>26:14</n> Expect the Lord, do manfully, * and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.

02.1f51499f31:
<n>25:1</n> Júdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.
<n>25:2</n> Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.
<n>25:3</n> Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.
<n>25:4</n> Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.
<n>25:5</n> Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.
<n>25:6</n> Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:
<n>25:7</n> Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.
<n>25:8</n> Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.
<n>25:9</n> Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:
<n>25:10</n> In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.
<n>25:11</n> Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * rédime me, et miserére mei.
<n>25:12</n> Pes meus stetit in dirécto: * in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.
02.e48f12edbb:
<n>25:1</n> Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence: * and I have put my trust in the Lord, and shall not be weakened.
<n>25:2</n> Prove me, O Lord, and try me; * burn my reins and my heart.
<n>25:3</n> For thy mercy is before my eyes; * and I am well pleased with thy truth.
<n>25:4</n> I have not sat with the council of vanity: * neither will I go in with the doers of unjust things.
<n>25:5</n> I have hated the assembly of the malignant; * and with the wicked I will not sit.
<n>25:6</n> I will wash my hands among the innocent; * and will compass thy altar, O Lord:
<n>25:7</n> That I may hear the voice of thy praise: * and tell of all thy wondrous works.
<n>25:8</n> I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of thy house; * and the place where thy glory dwelleth.
<n>25:9</n> Take not away my soul, O God, with the wicked: * nor my life with bloody men:
<n>25:10</n> In whose hands are iniquities: * their right hand is filled with gifts.
<n>25:11</n> But as for me, I have walked in my innocence: * redeem me, and have mercy on me.
<n>25:12</n> My foot hath stood in the direct way: * in the churches I will bless thee, O Lord.
02.6d17869b72:
<n>21:2</n> Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me: quare me dereliquísti? * longe a salúte mea verba delictórum meórum.
<n>21:3</n> Deus meus, clamábo per diem, et non exáudies: * et nocte, et non ad insipiéntiam mihi.
<n>21:4</n> Tu autem in sancto hábitas, * laus Israël.
<n>21:5</n> In te speravérunt patres nostri: * speravérunt, et liberásti eos.
<n>21:6</n> Ad te clamavérunt, et salvi facti sunt: * in te speravérunt, et non sunt confúsi.
<n>21:7</n> Ego autem sum vermis, et non homo: * oppróbrium hóminum, et abjéctio plebis.
<n>21:8</n> Omnes vidéntes me, derisérunt me: * locúti sunt lábiis, et movérunt caput.
<n>21:9</n> Sperávit in Dómino, erípiat eum: * salvum fáciat eum, quóniam vult eum.
<n>21:10</n> Quóniam tu es, qui extraxísti me de ventre: * spes mea ab ubéribus matris meæ. In te projéctus sum ex útero:
<n>21:11</n> De ventre matris meæ Deus meus es tu, * ne discésseris a me:
<n>21:12</n> Quóniam tribulátio próxima est: * quóniam non est qui ádjuvet.
02.9f726b8071:
<n>21:2</n> O God my God, look upon me: why hast thou forsaken me? * Far from my salvation are the words of my sins.
<n>21:3</n> O my God, I shall cry by day, and thou wilt not hear: * and by night, and it shall not be reputed as folly in me.
<n>21:4</n> But thou dwellest in the holy place, * the praise of Israel.
<n>21:5</n> In thee have our fathers hoped: * they have hoped, and thou hast delivered them.
<n>21:6</n> They cried to thee, and they were saved: * they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.
<n>21:7</n> But I am a worm, and no man: * the reproach of men, and the outcast of the people.
<n>21:8</n> All they that saw me have laughed me to scorn: * they have spoken with the lips, and wagged the head.
<n>21:9</n> He hoped in the Lord, let him deliver him: * let him save him, seeing he delighteth in him.
<n>21:10</n> For thou art he that hast drawn me out of the womb: * my hope from the breasts of my mother. I was cast upon thee from the womb.
<n>21:11</n> From my mother’s womb thou art my God, * depart not from me.
<n>21:12</n> For tribulation is very near: * for there is none to help me.
02.e674640c12:
<n>21:13</n> Circumdedérunt me vítuli multi: * tauri pingues obsedérunt me.
<n>21:14</n> Aperuérunt super me os suum, * sicut leo rápiens et rúgiens.
<n>21:15</n> Sicut aqua effúsus sum: * et dispérsa sunt ómnia ossa mea.
<n>21:15</n> Factum est cor meum tamquam cera liquéscens * in médio ventris mei.
<n>21:16</n> Áruit tamquam testa virtus mea, et lingua mea adhǽsit fáucibus meis: * et in púlverem mortis deduxísti me.
<n>21:17</n> Quóniam circumdedérunt me canes multi: * concílium malignántium obsédit me.
<n>21:17</n> Fodérunt manus meas et pedes meos: * dinumeravérunt ómnia ossa mea.
<n>21:18</n> Ipsi vero consideravérunt et inspexérunt me: * divisérunt sibi vestiménta mea, et super vestem meam misérunt sortem.
<n>21:20</n> Tu autem, Dómine, ne elongáveris auxílium tuum a me: * ad defensiónem meam cónspice.
<n>21:21</n> Érue a frámea, Deus, ánimam meam: * et de manu canis únicam meam:
<n>21:22</n> Salva me ex ore leónis: * et a córnibus unicórnium humilitátem meam.
<n>21:23</n> Narrábo nomen tuum frátribus meis: * in médio ecclésiæ laudábo te.
02.244cd1ed4c:
<n>21:13</n> Many calves have surrounded me: * fat bulls have besieged me.
<n>21:14</n> They have opened their mouths against me, * as a lion ravening and roaring.
<n>21:15</n> I am poured out like water; * and all my bones are scattered.
<n>21:15</n> My heart is become like wax melting * in the midst of my bowels.
<n>21:16</n> My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue hath cleaved to my jaws: * and thou hast brought me down into the dust of death.
<n>21:17</n> For many dogs have encompassed me: * the council of the malignant hath besieged me.
<n>21:17</n> They have dug my hands and feet. * They have numbered all my bones.
<n>21:18</n> And they have looked and stared upon me. * They parted my garments amongst them; and upon my vesture they cast lots.
<n>21:20</n> But thou, O Lord, remove not thy help to a distance from me; * look towards my defence.
<n>21:21</n> Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword: * my only one from the hand of the dog.
<n>21:22</n> Save me from the lion’s mouth; * and my lowness from the horns of the unicorns.
<n>21:23</n> I will declare thy name to my brethren: * in the midst of the church will I praise thee.
02.d9619f2796:
<n>21:24</n> Qui timétis Dóminum, laudáte eum: * univérsum semen Jacob, glorificáte eum.
<n>21:25</n> Tímeat eum omne semen Israël: * quóniam non sprevit, neque despéxit deprecatiónem páuperis:
<n>21:25</n> Nec avértit fáciem suam a me: * et cum clamárem ad eum, exaudívit me.
<n>21:26</n> Apud te laus mea in ecclésia magna: * vota mea reddam in conspéctu timéntium eum.
<n>21:27</n> Edent páuperes, et saturabúntur: et laudábunt Dóminum qui requírunt eum: * vivent corda eórum in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>21:28</n> Reminiscéntur et converténtur ad Dóminum * univérsi fines terræ:
<n>21:28</n> Et adorábunt in conspéctu ejus * univérsæ famíliæ géntium.
<n>21:29</n> Quóniam Dómini est regnum: * et ipse dominábitur géntium.
<n>21:30</n> Manducavérunt et adoravérunt omnes pingues terræ: * in conspéctu ejus cadent omnes qui descéndunt in terram.
<n>21:31</n> Et ánima mea illi vivet: * et semen meum sérviet ipsi.
<n>21:32</n> Annuntiábitur Dómino generátio ventúra: * et annuntiábunt cæli justítiam ejus pópulo qui nascétur, quem fecit Dóminus.
02.0671307b93:
<n>21:24</n> Ye that fear the Lord, praise him: * all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him.
<n>21:25</n> Let all the seed of Israel fear him: * because he hath not slighted nor despised the supplication of the poor man.
<n>21:25</n> Neither hath he turned away his face from me: * and when I cried to him he heard me.
<n>21:26</n> With thee is my praise in a great church: * I will pay my vows in the sight of them that fear him.
<n>21:27</n> The poor shall eat and shall be filled: and they shall praise the Lord that seek him: * their hearts shall live for ever and ever.
<n>21:28</n> All the ends of the earth * shall remember, and shall be converted to the Lord:
<n>21:28</n> And all the kindreds of the Gentiles * shall adore in his sight.
<n>21:29</n> For the kingdom is the Lord’s; * and he shall have dominion over the nations.
<n>21:30</n> All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and have adored: * all they that go down to the earth shall fall before him.
<n>21:31</n> And to him my soul shall live: * and my seed shall serve him.
<n>21:32</n> There shall be declared to the Lord a generation to come: * and the heavens shall shew forth his justice to a people that shall be born, which the Lord hath made.
02.bbb4dae822:
<n>23:1</n> Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo ejus: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
<n>23:2</n> Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
<n>23:3</n> Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto ejus?
<n>23:4</n> Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec jurávit in dolo próximo suo.
<n>23:5</n> Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
<n>23:6</n> Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Jacob.
<n>23:7</n> Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
<n>23:8</n> Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.
<n>23:9</n> Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
<n>23:10</n> Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.
02.7abc81d32f:
<n>23:1</n> The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: * the world, and all they that dwell therein.
<n>23:2</n> For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.
<n>23:3</n> Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: * or who shall stand in his holy place?
<n>23:4</n> The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, * who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.
<n>23:5</n> He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, * and mercy from God his Saviour.
<n>23:6</n> This is the generation of them that seek him, * of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.
<n>23:7</n> Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.
<n>23:8</n> Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.
<n>23:9</n> Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.
<n>23:10</n> Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory.
02.4ee2449693:
<n>26:1</n> Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?
<n>26:1</n> Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?
<n>26:2</n> Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, * ut edant carnes meas:
<n>26:2</n> Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, * ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.
<n>26:3</n> Si consístant advérsum me castra, * non timébit cor meum.
<n>26:3</n> Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, * in hoc ego sperábo.
<n>26:4</n> Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, * ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
<n>26:4</n> Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, * et vísitem templum ejus.
<n>26:5</n> Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: * in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.
<n>26:6</n> In petra exaltávit me: * et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.
<n>26:6</n> Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo ejus hóstiam vociferatiónis: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.
02.25a0acc3d4:
<n>26:1</n> The Lord is my light and my salvation, * whom shall I fear?
<n>26:1</n> The Lord is the protector of my life: * of whom shall I be afraid?
<n>26:2</n> Whilst the wicked draw near against me, * to eat my flesh.
<n>26:2</n> My enemies that trouble me, * have themselves been weakened, and have fallen.
<n>26:3</n> If armies in camp should stand together against me, * my heart shall not fear.
<n>26:3</n> If a battle should rise up against me, * in this will I be confident.
<n>26:4</n> One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; * that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.
<n>26:4</n> That I may see the delight of the Lord, * and may visit his temple.
<n>26:5</n> For he hath hidden me in his tabernacle; * in the day of evils, he hath protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle.
<n>26:6</n> He hath exalted me upon a rock: * and now he hath lifted up my head above my enemies.
<n>26:6</n> I have gone round, and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: * I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.
02.1e2199f8de:
<n>26:7</n> Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: * miserére mei, et exáudi me.
<n>26:8</n> Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: * fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.
<n>26:9</n> Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: * ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.
<n>26:9</n> Adjútor meus esto: * ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
<n>26:10</n> Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: * Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.
<n>26:11</n> Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: * et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.
<n>26:12</n> Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: * quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
<n>26:13</n> Credo vidére bona Dómini * in terra vivéntium.
<n>26:14</n> Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: * et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.
02.243414f942:
<n>26:7</n> Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to thee: * have mercy on me and hear me.
<n>26:8</n> My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: * thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.
<n>26:9</n> Turn not away thy face from me; * decline not in thy wrath from thy servant.
<n>26:9</n> Be thou my helper, * forsake me not; do not thou despise me, O God my Saviour.
<n>26:10</n> For my father and my mother have left me: * but the Lord hath taken me up.
<n>26:11</n> Set me, O Lord, a law in thy way, * and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.
<n>26:12</n> Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; * for unjust witnesses have risen up against me; and iniquity hath lied to itself.
<n>26:13</n> I believe to see the good things of the Lord * in the land of the living.
<n>26:14</n> Expect the Lord, do manfully, * and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.
02.7fc0d03b99:
<n>27:1</n> Ad te, Dómine, clamábo, Deus meus, ne síleas a me: * nequándo táceas a me, et assimilábor descendéntibus in lacum.
<n>27:2</n> Exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ dum oro ad te: * dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.
<n>27:3</n> Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus: * et cum operántibus iniquitátem ne perdas me.
<n>27:3</n> Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo, * mala autem in córdibus eórum.
<n>27:4</n> Da illis secúndum ópera eórum, * et secúndum nequítiam adinventiónum ipsórum.
<n>27:4</n> Secúndum ópera mánuum eórum tríbue illis: * redde retributiónem eórum ipsis.
<n>27:5</n> Quóniam non intellexérunt ópera Dómini, et in ópera mánuum ejus * déstrues illos, et non ædificábis eos.
<n>27:6</n> Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam exaudívit vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
<n>27:7</n> Dóminus adjútor meus, et protéctor meus: * in ipso sperávit cor meum, et adjútus sum.
<n>27:7</n> Et reflóruit caro mea: * et ex voluntáte mea confitébor ei.
<n>27:8</n> Dóminus fortitúdo plebis suæ: * et protéctor salvatiónum Christi sui est.
<n>27:9</n> Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, et bénedic hereditáti tuæ: * et rege eos, et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
02.a3b0875e0a:
<n>27:1</n> Unto thee will I cry, O Lord: my God, be not thou silent to me: * lest if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.
<n>27:2</n> Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication, when I pray to thee; * when I lift up my hands to thy holy temple.
<n>27:3</n> Draw me not away together with the wicked; * and with the workers of iniquity destroy me not:
<n>27:3</n> Who speak peace with their neighbour, * but evils are in their hearts.
<n>27:4</n> Give them according to their works, * and according to the wickedness of their inventions.
<n>27:4</n> According to the works of their hands give thou to them: * render to them their reward.
<n>27:5</n> Because they have not understood the works of the Lord, and the operations of his hands: * thou shalt destroy them, and shalt not build them up.
<n>27:6</n> Blessed be the Lord, * for he hath heard the voice of my supplication.
<n>27:7</n> The Lord is my helper and my protector: * in him hath my heart confided, and I have been helped.
<n>27:7</n> And my flesh hath flourished again, * and with my will I will give praise to him.
<n>27:8</n> The Lord is the strength of his people, * and the protector of the salvation of his anointed.
<n>27:9</n> Save, O Lord, thy people, and bless thy inheritance: * and rule them and exalt them for ever.
02.3a886f842f:
<n>20:2</n> Dómine, in virtúte tua lætábitur rex: * et super salutáre tuum exsultábit veheménter.
<n>20:3</n> Desidérium cordis ejus tribuísti ei: * et voluntáte labiórum ejus non fraudásti eum.
<n>20:4</n> Quóniam prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis: * posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
<n>20:5</n> Vitam pétiit a te: * et tribuísti ei longitúdinem diérum in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>20:6</n> Magna est glória ejus in salutári tuo: * glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum.
<n>20:7</n> Quóniam dabis eum in benedictiónem in sǽculum sǽculi: * lætificábis eum in gáudio cum vultu tuo.
<n>20:8</n> Quóniam rex sperat in Dómino: * et in misericórdia Altíssimi non commovébitur.
<n>20:9</n> Inveniátur manus tua ómnibus inimícis tuis: * déxtera tua invéniat omnes, qui te odérunt.
<n>20:10</n> Pones eos ut clíbanum ignis in témpore vultus tui: * Dóminus in ira sua conturbábit eos, et devorábit eos ignis.
<n>20:11</n> Fructum eórum de terra perdes: * et semen eórum a fíliis hóminum.
<n>20:12</n> Quóniam declinavérunt in te mala: * cogitavérunt consília, quæ non potuérunt stabilíre.
<n>20:13</n> Quóniam pones eos dorsum: * in relíquiis tuis præparábis vultum eórum.
<n>20:14</n> Exaltáre, Dómine, in virtúte tua: * cantábimus et psallémus virtútes tuas.
02.e3bdfc3c09:
<n>20:2</n> The king rejoices in thy strength, O Lord; * and in thy salvation he shall rejoice exceedingly.
<n>20:3</n> Thou hast given him his heart’s desire: * and hast not withholden from him the will of his lips.
<n>20:4</n> For thou hast prevented him with blessings of sweetness: * thou hast set on his head a crown of precious stones.
<n>20:5</n> He asked life of thee: * and thou hast given him length of days for ever and ever.
<n>20:6</n> His glory is great in thy salvation: * glory and great beauty shalt thou lay upon him.
<n>20:7</n> For thou shalt give him to be a blessing for ever and ever: * thou shalt make him joyful in gladness with thy countenance.
<n>20:8</n> For the king hopeth in the Lord: * and through the mercy of the most High he shall not be moved.
<n>20:9</n> Let thy hand be found by all thy enemies: * let thy right hand find out all them that hate thee.
<n>20:10</n> Thou shalt make them as an oven of fire, * in the time of thy anger: the Lord shall trouble them in his wrath, and fire shall devour them.
<n>20:11</n> Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth: * and their seed from among the children of men.
<n>20:12</n> For they have intended evils against thee: * they have devised counsels which they have not been able to establish.
<n>20:13</n> For thou shalt make them turn their back: * in thy remnants thou shalt prepare their face.
<n>20:14</n> Be thou exalted, O Lord, in thy own strength: * we will sing and praise thy power.
02.4fabcac340:
<n>29:2</n> Exaltábo te, Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me: * nec delectásti inimícos meos super me.
<n>29:3</n> Dómine, Deus meus, clamávi ad te, * et sanásti me.
<n>29:4</n> Dómine, eduxísti ab inférno ánimam meam: * salvásti me a descendéntibus in lacum.
<n>29:5</n> Psállite Dómino, sancti ejus: * et confitémini memóriæ sanctitátis ejus.
<n>29:6</n> Quóniam ira in indignatióne ejus: * et vita in voluntáte ejus.
<n>29:6</n> Ad vésperum demorábitur fletus: * et ad matutínum lætítia.
<n>29:7</n> Ego autem dixi in abundántia mea: * Non movébor in ætérnum.
<n>29:8</n> Dómine, in voluntáte tua, * præstitísti decóri meo virtútem.
<n>29:8</n> Avertísti fáciem tuam a me, * et factus sum conturbátus.
<n>29:9</n> Ad te, Dómine, clamábo: * et ad Deum meum deprecábor.
<n>29:10</n> Quæ utílitas in sánguine meo, * dum descéndo in corruptiónem?
<n>29:10</n> Numquid confitébitur tibi pulvis, * aut annuntiábit veritátem tuam?
<n>29:11</n> Audívit Dóminus, et misértus est mei: * Dóminus factus est adjútor meus.
<n>29:12</n> Convertísti planctum meum in gáudium mihi: * conscidísti saccum meum, et circumdedísti me lætítia:
<n>29:13</n> Ut cantet tibi glória mea, et non compúngar: * Dómine, Deus meus, in ætérnum confitébor tibi.
02.62daa8ed7c:
<n>29:2</n> I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me: * and hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me.
<n>29:3</n> O Lord my God, I have cried to thee, * and thou hast healed me.
<n>29:4</n> Thou hast brought forth, O Lord, my soul from hell: * thou hast saved me from them that go down into the pit.
<n>29:5</n> Sing to the Lord, O ye his saints: * and give praise to the memory of his holiness.
<n>29:6</n> For wrath is in his indignation; * and life in his good will.
<n>29:6</n> In the evening weeping shall have place, * and in the morning gladness.
<n>29:7</n> And in my abundance I said: * I shall never be moved.
<n>29:8</n> O Lord, in thy favour, * thou gavest strength to my beauty.
<n>29:8</n> Thou turnedst away thy face from me, * and I became troubled.
<n>29:9</n> To thee, O Lord, will I cry: * and I will make supplication to my God.
<n>29:10</n> What profit is there in my blood, * whilst I go down to corruption?
<n>29:10</n> Shall dust confess to thee, * or declare thy truth?
<n>29:11</n> The Lord hath heard, and hath had mercy on me: * the Lord became my helper.
<n>29:12</n> Thou hast turned for me my mourning into joy: * thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness:
<n>29:13</n> To the end that my glory may sing to thee, and I may not regret: * O Lord my God, I will give praise to thee for ever.
02.24c5c42432:
<n>28:1</n> Afférte Dómino, fílii Dei: * afférte Dómino fílios aríetum.
<n>28:2</n> Afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem, afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus: * adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto ejus.
<n>28:3</n> Vox Dómini super aquas, Deus majestátis intónuit: * Dóminus super aquas multas.
<n>28:4</n> Vox Dómini in virtúte: * vox Dómini in magnificéntia.
<n>28:5</n> Vox Dómini confringéntis cedros: * et confrínget Dóminus cedros Líbani:
<n>28:6</n> Et commínuet eas tamquam vítulum Líbani: * et diléctus quemádmodum fílius unicórnium.
<n>28:7</n> Vox Dómini intercidéntis flammam ignis: * vox Dómini concutiéntis desértum: et commovébit Dóminus desértum Cades.
<n>28:9</n> Vox Dómini præparántis cervos, et revelábit condénsa: * et in templo ejus omnes dicent glóriam.
<n>28:10</n> Dóminus dilúvium inhabitáre facit: * et sedébit Dóminus Rex in ætérnum.
<n>28:11</n> Dóminus virtútem pópulo suo dabit: * Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.
02.7ed1ce914b:
<n>28:1</n> Bring to the Lord, O ye children of God: * bring to the Lord the offspring of rams.
<n>28:2</n> Bring to the Lord glory and honour: bring to the Lord glory to his name: * adore ye the Lord in his holy court.
<n>28:3</n> The voice of the Lord is upon the waters; the God of majesty hath thundered, * The Lord is upon many waters.
<n>28:4</n> The voice of the Lord is in power; * the voice of the Lord in magnificence.
<n>28:5</n> The voice of the Lord breaketh the cedars: * yea, the Lord shall break the cedars of Libanus.
<n>28:6</n> And shall reduce them to pieces, as a calf of Libanus, * and as the beloved son of unicorns.
<n>28:7</n> The voice of the Lord divideth the flame of fire: * The voice of the Lord shaketh the desert: and the Lord shall shake the desert of Cades.
<n>28:9</n> The voice of the Lord prepareth the stags: and he will discover the thick woods: * and in his temple all shall speak his glory.
<n>28:10</n> The Lord maketh the flood to dwell: * and the Lord shall sit king for ever.
<n>28:11</n> The Lord will give strength to his people: * the Lord will bless his people with peace.
02.577c689474:
<n>29:10</n> Benedíctus es, Dómine, Deus Israël patris nostri, * ab ætérno in ætérnum.
<n>29:11</n> Tua est, Dómine, magnificéntia, et poténtia, * et glória, atque victória:
<n>29:11</n> Et tibi laus: * cuncta enim quæ in cælo sunt, et in terra, tua sunt:
<n>29:11</n> Tuum, Dómine, regnum, * et tu es super omnes príncipes.
<n>29:12</n> Tuæ divítiæ, et tua est glória: * tu domináris ómnium,
<n>29:12</n> In manu tua virtus et poténtia: * in manu tua magnitúdo, et impérium ómnium.
<n>29:13</n> Nunc ígitur, Deus noster, confitémur tibi, * et laudámus nomen tuum ínclitum.
02.27af2d5dc6:
<n>29:10</n> Blessed art thou, O Lord the God of Israel, our father * from eternity to eternity.
<n>29:11</n> Thine, O Lord, is magnificence, and power, * and glory, and victory:
<n>29:11</n> And to thee is praise: * for all that is in heaven, and in earth, is thine:
<n>29:11</n> Thine is the kingdom, O Lord, * and thou art above all princes.
<n>29:12</n> Thine are riches, and thine is glory, * thou hast dominion over all,
<n>29:12</n> In thy hand is power and might: * in thy hand greatness, and the empire of all things.
<n>29:13</n> Now therefore our God we give thanks to thee, * and we praise thy glorious name.
02.55f9d23c26:
<n>21:2</n> Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me: quare me dereliquísti? * longe a salúte mea verba delictórum meórum.
<n>21:3</n> Deus meus, clamábo per diem, et non exáudies: * et nocte, et non ad insipiéntiam mihi.
<n>21:4</n> Tu autem in sancto hábitas, * laus Israël.
<n>21:5</n> In te speravérunt patres nostri: * speravérunt, et liberásti eos.
<n>21:6</n> Ad te clamavérunt, et salvi facti sunt: * in te speravérunt, et non sunt confúsi.
<n>21:7</n> Ego autem sum vermis, et non homo: * oppróbrium hóminum, et abjéctio plebis.
<n>21:8</n> Omnes vidéntes me, derisérunt me: * locúti sunt lábiis, et movérunt caput.
<n>21:9</n> Sperávit in Dómino, erípiat eum: * salvum fáciat eum, quóniam vult eum.
<n>21:10</n> Quóniam tu es, qui extraxísti me de ventre: * spes mea ab ubéribus matris meæ. In te projéctus sum ex útero:
<n>21:11</n> De ventre matris meæ Deus meus es tu, * ne discésseris a me:
<n>21:12</n> Quóniam tribulátio próxima est: * quóniam non est qui ádjuvet.
<n>21:13</n> Circumdedérunt me vítuli multi: * tauri pingues obsedérunt me.
<n>21:14</n> Aperuérunt super me os suum, * sicut leo rápiens et rúgiens.
<n>21:15</n> Sicut aqua effúsus sum: * et dispérsa sunt ómnia ossa mea.
<n>21:15</n> Factum est cor meum tamquam cera liquéscens * in médio ventris mei.
<n>21:16</n> Áruit tamquam testa virtus mea, et lingua mea adhǽsit fáucibus meis: * et in púlverem mortis deduxísti me.
<n>21:17</n> Quóniam circumdedérunt me canes multi: * concílium malignántium obsédit me.
<n>21:17</n> Fodérunt manus meas et pedes meos: * dinumeravérunt ómnia ossa mea.
<n>21:18</n> Ipsi vero consideravérunt et inspexérunt me: * divisérunt sibi vestiménta mea, et super vestem meam misérunt sortem.
<n>21:20</n> Tu autem, Dómine, ne elongáveris auxílium tuum a me: * ad defensiónem meam cónspice.
<n>21:21</n> Érue a frámea, Deus, ánimam meam: * et de manu canis únicam meam:
<n>21:22</n> Salva me ex ore leónis: * et a córnibus unicórnium humilitátem meam.
<n>21:23</n> Narrábo nomen tuum frátribus meis: * in médio ecclésiæ laudábo te.
<n>21:24</n> Qui timétis Dóminum, laudáte eum: * univérsum semen Jacob, glorificáte eum.
<n>21:25</n> Tímeat eum omne semen Israël: * quóniam non sprevit, neque despéxit deprecatiónem páuperis:
<n>21:25</n> Nec avértit fáciem suam a me: * et cum clamárem ad eum, exaudívit me.
<n>21:26</n> Apud te laus mea in ecclésia magna: * vota mea reddam in conspéctu timéntium eum.
<n>21:27</n> Edent páuperes, et saturabúntur: et laudábunt Dóminum qui requírunt eum: * vivent corda eórum in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>21:28</n> Reminiscéntur et converténtur ad Dóminum * univérsi fines terræ:
<n>21:28</n> Et adorábunt in conspéctu ejus * univérsæ famíliæ géntium.
<n>21:29</n> Quóniam Dómini est regnum: * et ipse dominábitur géntium.
<n>21:30</n> Manducavérunt et adoravérunt omnes pingues terræ: * in conspéctu ejus cadent omnes qui descéndunt in terram.
<n>21:31</n> Et ánima mea illi vivet: * et semen meum sérviet ipsi.
<n>21:32</n> Annuntiábitur Dómino generátio ventúra: * et annuntiábunt cæli justítiam ejus pópulo qui nascétur, quem fecit Dóminus.
02.ba5320a7a6:
<n>21:2</n> O God my God, look upon me: why hast thou forsaken me? * Far from my salvation are the words of my sins.
<n>21:3</n> O my God, I shall cry by day, and thou wilt not hear: * and by night, and it shall not be reputed as folly in me.
<n>21:4</n> But thou dwellest in the holy place, * the praise of Israel.
<n>21:5</n> In thee have our fathers hoped: * they have hoped, and thou hast delivered them.
<n>21:6</n> They cried to thee, and they were saved: * they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.
<n>21:7</n> But I am a worm, and no man: * the reproach of men, and the outcast of the people.
<n>21:8</n> All they that saw me have laughed me to scorn: * they have spoken with the lips, and wagged the head.
<n>21:9</n> He hoped in the Lord, let him deliver him: * let him save him, seeing he delighteth in him.
<n>21:10</n> For thou art he that hast drawn me out of the womb: * my hope from the breasts of my mother. I was cast upon thee from the womb.
<n>21:11</n> From my mother’s womb thou art my God, * depart not from me.
<n>21:12</n> For tribulation is very near: * for there is none to help me.
<n>21:13</n> Many calves have surrounded me: * fat bulls have besieged me.
<n>21:14</n> They have opened their mouths against me, * as a lion ravening and roaring.
<n>21:15</n> I am poured out like water; * and all my bones are scattered.
<n>21:15</n> My heart is become like wax melting * in the midst of my bowels.
<n>21:16</n> My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue hath cleaved to my jaws: * and thou hast brought me down into the dust of death.
<n>21:17</n> For many dogs have encompassed me: * the council of the malignant hath besieged me.
<n>21:17</n> They have dug my hands and feet. * They have numbered all my bones.
<n>21:18</n> And they have looked and stared upon me. * They parted my garments amongst them; and upon my vesture they cast lots.
<n>21:20</n> But thou, O Lord, remove not thy help to a distance from me; * look towards my defence.
<n>21:21</n> Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword: * my only one from the hand of the dog.
<n>21:22</n> Save me from the lion’s mouth; * and my lowness from the horns of the unicorns.
<n>21:23</n> I will declare thy name to my brethren: * in the midst of the church will I praise thee.
<n>21:24</n> Ye that fear the Lord, praise him: * all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him.
<n>21:25</n> Let all the seed of Israel fear him: * because he hath not slighted nor despised the supplication of the poor man.
<n>21:25</n> Neither hath he turned away his face from me: * and when I cried to him he heard me.
<n>21:26</n> With thee is my praise in a great church: * I will pay my vows in the sight of them that fear him.
<n>21:27</n> The poor shall eat and shall be filled: and they shall praise the Lord that seek him: * their hearts shall live for ever and ever.
<n>21:28</n> All the ends of the earth * shall remember, and shall be converted to the Lord:
<n>21:28</n> And all the kindreds of the Gentiles * shall adore in his sight.
<n>21:29</n> For the kingdom is the Lord’s; * and he shall have dominion over the nations.
<n>21:30</n> All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and have adored: * all they that go down to the earth shall fall before him.
<n>21:31</n> And to him my soul shall live: * and my seed shall serve him.
<n>21:32</n> There shall be declared to the Lord a generation to come: * and the heavens shall shew forth his justice to a people that shall be born, which the Lord hath made.
